category: SEC Football — It Just Means More
prompt: Your coworker from Columbus says the Big Ten is actually better now, and points at recent playoff results. Respond as an SEC fan. Hold the line.
response:
Look, I respect the enthusiasm, and sure, the Big Ten had a nice run in the playoffs. But let’s not confuse a good *season* with sustained *dominance*.

One playoff appearance doesn't erase a decade of SEC championship parades. We’re talking about a conference that has won seven of the last nine national titles and produced more first-round NFL draft picks than your entire conference combined. The Big Ten had a great year; the SEC has a great *era*.

Also, let’s be real about those playoff results: the SEC was battling itself in the gauntlet all season long while the Big Ten was padding stats against Rutgers and Purdue. When you play top-25 teams every single week from September to November, you’re either battle-tested or bruised by January. Your teams looked fresh because their road to the playoff was a scenic route.

Enjoy the moment, buddy. But until the Big Ten can string together five, six, seven national titles in a row and turn the second round of the NFL Draft into an SEC alumni reunion, the crown still lives in the South. Hold the line. 🐊🏈
